assertions.evidence: Multiple rows show blank cells for Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns (e.g., 'Valid registration, optional fields omitted' row).

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column

assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Accepted?, Error?, Discount?, Price?

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Name', 'Email', 'Registration date', 'Group size', 'Price?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Columns named 'Name', 'Email', 'Dietary Requirements', 'Accessibility Needs', 'Registration Date', 'Group Size', 'Discount?', 'Price?' — all business language.

assertions.evidence: Scenarios named 'Missing name', 'Email missing @ symbol', 'Early-bird registration', 'Group of 5 or more qualifies for group discount' — all describe conditions, not outcomes.

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 2 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: 'shouldValidateRegistration' and 'shouldCalculateDiscountAndPrice', each addressing validation and pricing respectively.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Validation table has 9 rows including multiple email format variants (missing @, missing local part, missing domain, no TLD) and blank/whitespace name variants. Pricing table has 5 rows with value sets {1,2,3,4} and {5,6,20} creating implicit permutations rather than minimal distinct cases.

assertions.text: Input validation and pricing/discount calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: Two methods: 'shouldValidateRegistration' for validation and 'shouldCalculateDiscountAndPrice' for pricing, clearly separated.

assertions.text: Validation @TableTest includes Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns, with rows showing both null (blank) and non-null values are accepted — not hardcoded as null in the method body.
assertions.evidence: Validation table has 'Dietary Requirements' and 'Accessibility Needs' columns; 'Valid registration, optional fields provided' row shows non-null values (Vegetarian, Wheelchair access); other rows show blanks.

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values (e.g. 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff') with a @TypeConverter method converting to actual dates — not raw date literals like '2025-02-28'. Readability over precision.
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter parseRegistrationDate method converts 'just before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff' to LocalDate values; pricing table uses these descriptive strings, not literals.

assertions.text: If registration dates are literal (e.g. '2025-02-28' instead of descriptive), the early-bird cutoff date appears as a separate policy column so the reader can see both dates and verify the comparison. Passes automatically if descriptive date values are used.
assertions.evidence: Descriptive date values used: 'just before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff' via @TypeConverter; no literal dates in table.

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it does not include information already visible in the table columns or derivable from the table structure — such as fixed input values that could be columns, or restating a rule the rows already demonstrate. It PASSES when the description adds what the rows cannot: a threshold or constant fixed in the method body, currency, where/when the rule applies, or naming an interpretation as a deliberate assumption.
assertions.evidence: Pricing @Description states 'Base price is £100' (constant fixed in method body, not a column), 'Cutoff date is 2025-03-01' (policy constant), and 'Price = Base Price - Discount' (the operation). Validation @Description explains why date/group are fixed (irrelevant to validation concern).

assertions.text: Output column is 'Discount?' (percentage or amount off) rather than 'Price?' — making verification simpler (discount is the rule's direct output; price requires knowing the base price). If 'Price?' is used instead, both 'Base price' and 'Price?' columns must be present so the reader can trace the calculation.
assertions.evidence: Both 'Discount?' and 'Price?' columns present; Discount is the direct output, Price is derived. @Description states 'Base price is £100' and 'Price = Base Price - Discount', enabling traceability.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method applies one uniform assertion pattern to every row — not different assertions per scenario. Several unconditional assertions checking distinct observable outputs of one result (e.g. success, message, resulting cart) count as one uniform pattern; the anti-pattern is branching on the row (if/switch/ternary/try-catch) to choose what is asserted.
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) apply one uniform assertion pattern to all rows

assertions.text: The optional-fields acceptance table includes an expectation/output column (e.g. 'Approved?', 'Result?', or 'Status?') asserting that each combination is accepted — not just varying inputs without any expected column.
assertions.evidence: Validation table includes 'Accepted?' and 'Error?' output columns; rows assert acceptance (true/false) and error messages for each input combination.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description text do not restate values the table already shows. The assertion FAILS if either: (1) a scenario name contains a literal value that also appears in an input cell of the same row (e.g. scenario 'Age 35, score 700' beside Age and Credit score columns holding 35 and 700); or (2) @Description states a fixed value for an input that is already a column in that table. Otherwise it PASSES.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names describe conditions ('Early-bird registration', 'Group of 5 or more') without restating literal cell values. @Description fixes constants (£100 base, 2025-03-01 cutoff) that are not columns; date/group are fixed in method body, not described as column values.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable. Judge each @TableTest table independently; the assertion FAILS if any table meets any of these conditions: (1) its expectation column holds the same value in every row; (2) in every row, each expectation cell is a verbatim copy of a cell in an input column of the same row; (3) an implementation that ignored the input columns entirely and returned a fixed value would satisfy every row. Otherwise the assertion PASSES.
assertions.evidence: Validation: 'Accepted?' varies (true/false); 'Error?' varies (null, specific messages). Pricing: 'Discount?' varies (0.00, 20.00, 15.00); 'Price?' varies (100.00, 80.00, 85.00). No row's expectation is a copy of an input cell.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body. The assertion FAILS if any of these hold for any @TableTest: (1) a value needed to predict the expectation (a threshold, rate, cutoff, multiplier, reference date) appears only in the method body or a field, and in neither a column, the @DisplayName, nor the @Description; (2) the operation applied to the inputs cannot be named from the column headers and cell values alone; (3) a helper method used in the assertion applies a comparison criterion (ordering, tolerance, subset matching) that is stated nowhere in the table, title, or description. Otherwise the assertion PASSES.
assertions.evidence: Cutoff date (2025-03-01) stated in @Description. Base price (£100) stated in @Description. Group threshold (≥5) evident from rows (1–4 → 0%, 5+ → 15%). Early-bird rate (20%), group rate (15%), and max-not-sum rule all demonstrated by rows. @TypeConverter named in method signature; comparison uses BigDecimal.compareTo (standard equality, not a hidden tolerance).
